title: Jet Pilot Helmet with Visor and Oxygen Mask
finished_size_cm: 10.5 x 7 x 6 (depth including mask x width x height)
yarn_note: Made with light (DK, CYC 3) yarn and a smaller 3.0 mm hook, so the fabric is tight and the stuffing does not show through. The finished size is based on this yarn and hook; a thinner or thicker yarn makes the piece smaller or larger, so check your gauge first.

other: optional: 15 cm pipe cleaner for the hose

abbreviations.inc: increase (2 sc in the same st)

steps.instruction: (sc 4, dec) x 6. Start stuffing firmly and keep adding as you go.
dec x 6. Fasten off, weave the tail through the front loops and pull closed.
(sc 4, inc) x 6. Change to tan at the end of the rnd.
sc around. Sl st into the next st, fasten off and leave a long tail. The disc stays flat.
dec x 6. Stuff lightly, fasten off and leave a long tail.
sc around. Sl st into the next st, fasten off and leave a long tail. Do not stuff; the disc will curve like a visor when sewn on.
ch 21, sc in the 2nd ch from hook and in each ch across
ch 1, turn, sc in each st across. Fasten off and leave a long tail.
dec x 6. Fasten off, leave a long tail and close the hole.
sc around. Work every even-numbered rnd in BLO to create a ribbed, corrugated look. Stuff lightly as you go, or slip in a pipe cleaner. Fasten off and leave a long tail.

assembly: Pin the face opening disc to the lower front of the cream shell, so the tan rim frames the opening, and sew it on with the tail.
Sew the two black ear cups side by side onto the black centre of the disc.
Pin the visor over the upper front of the shell, covering the top of the face opening. Sew along its back edge only, so the front edge stands slightly proud like a raised visor.
Lay the orange stripe over the top centre of the shell, from the front edge of the visor to the back, and sew it down. Let it run under the visor edge.
Sew the olive mask just below the ear cups, at the bottom of the face opening, so it sticks out forward.
Sew one end of the hose to the back of the mask. Curve the hose in a loose loop and sew the other end to the side of the shell near the ear.
With tan yarn, embroider a chin strap in long straight stitches from the lower side edges of the shell. With olive yarn, embroider two short straps across the mask.
notes: Work all parts in a continuous spiral and mark the first st of each rnd. Change colour on the last pull-through of the final st of the previous rnd. Stuff the shell and mask firmly so they hold their shape. Keep the visor unstuffed, as it should stay thin and smooth.
